mechanism: One original native browser and immutable capability profile per runner worker; fresh ephemeral contexts for each test; original browser wait, observed group drain and native completed-write counters verified at worker teardown. Combined exclusion omits painting/capture, unused DOM storage, IndexedDB for TodoMVC only, and service workers; ordinary network and other storage remain.
attribution: Native journals are worker-lifetime records, not exact per-test native attribution. A caught violation fails worker teardown and the complete suite; individual test bodies may have passed before that error. Test metadata/context teardown records are separately joined to the reporter.

plan.hypothesis: Reusing one browser for compatible declarations removes per-attempt launch/recorder overhead; combined painting, DOM storage, IndexedDB and service-worker omissions may then affect complete suites.
plan.scope: Private homogeneous worker recording. Fresh context per test; immutable worker profile; native caught violations fail worker teardown and the complete suite. Native records belong to a worker lifetime, not individually attributed tests. This is not public per-test enforcement delivery.

profiles.fresh-full: Existing per-test browser recorder, full capabilities, discovery off.
profiles.reuse-full: One browser per runner worker, fresh context per test, full capabilities, discovery off.
profiles.reuse-restricted: Same reuse; painting/capture off; TodoMVC retains localStorage and other storage, SVGOMG retains IndexedDB and other storage; serviceWorker off; other capabilities on.

matrix.order: Nested order including profiles reversed in second block

plan.resourcePolicy: Serial systemd units; CPUQuota 400%; MemoryMax 8G; zero swap; retries 0; artifacts off.
plan.primaryMetric: Watchdog elapsed including application server, runner, original browser termination, native journal verification and observed drain; preparation outside owner interval.
plan.advancement: All controls and unchanged application outcomes/journals/cleanup must pass. Combined omission advances for broader performance work only if reuse-restricted reduces complete-owner time >=20% against reuse-full in at least 3 of 4 Flashwright application/worker cells in both blocks. Reuse vs fresh-full is recorder overhead attribution, not an engine advantage against ordinary Playwright.
limitations: Two blocks are an engineering screen, not confidence or population-tail admission.
Fresh contexts preserve per-test state boundaries; browser policy is process-global and worker-homogeneous.
Caught native violations are attributed to worker scope and fail the suite; no claim of exact per-test failure attribution.
No backend refresh or resource-custody admission.
Custom Linux no-sandbox browser and private file journal.

limitations: Two reversed blocks are an engineering screen, not confidence or population-tail admission.
Reuse versus fresh-full measures removal of recorder-imposed browser launches, not a new advantage over ordinary Playwright browser reuse.

Native records identify the worker lifetime; exact per-test attribution and production IPC remain unfinished. Reused original raw recorder descriptions still say per-test; wrapper worker metadata and this export explicitly narrow that attribution.
The private worker scope retains context records until worker teardown; bounded long-suite memory and production pool retirement are unverified.
Strict enforcement covers the previously tested selected boundary; broader implicit painting/storage/network dependencies remain open.
Both engines use the same custom Linux no-sandbox headless shell; no new browser build or public delivery.
Sampled resources and observed group drain do not prove exhaustive custody; three control writer PIDs escaped sampling.
No backend application refresh, portable packaging or release admission.
decision: Retain browser reuse as a requirement for any production capability implementation. Combined omission did not meet its selected complete-application advancement gate. Preserve the proven painting-heavy benefit separately; this screen neither rejects all possible declarations nor establishes the representative 2x objective.
